A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CamFormer study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary sections are readable and support comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original CamFormer experiments, including retrieval, classification, localization, robustness evaluations, and supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline evaluations and a quantitative analysis of trajectory geometry versus learned semantic similarity.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Supplementary Section 2.3 retain the relative 9D pose representation, Transformer encoder, contrastive alignment with frozen CLIP, contextualized pooling, and optional gravity token. The newly fine-tuned models are comparison baselines, not changes to CamFormer.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ego-Exo4D, Nymeria, DynPose-100K, FineGym, and UCF101, including its dynamic subset, with the same downstream task coverage. The added comparisons and embedding analysis use existing datasets and task settings.

E2.justification: Table 4 substantially broadens the comparison beyond two camera-description pipelines. It adds direct-trajectory zero-shot Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct and Gemini-3-Pro, plus supervised fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B and Qwen3-4B-Instruct, introducing both zero-shot and trained alternatives to the dedicated trajectory encoder.

E3.justification: Existing splits, MCQ construction, and CamFormer settings remain unchanged. New protocols include evaluating rendered trajectory videos or textual 9D sequences, fine-tuning baselines on DynPose-100K, and analyzing the most similar 1% of trajectory pairs from 5,000 Ego-Exo4D validation samples.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 3.1 adds a targeted semantic-disentanglement analysis testing whether geometrically similar trajectories remain similar after encoding and whether this separation corresponds to activity labels. Existing context-length, pose-source, representation, pretraining, and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added similarity and label-agreement percentages are point estimates, without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds accuracies of 21.5% for Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct, 24.7% for Gemini-3-Pro, 23.1% for SFT Qwen3-VL-4B, and 25.7% for SFT Qwen3-4B-Instruct; CamFormer remains at 36.2% and 46.3%. Supplementary Section 3.1 adds 1.61% similarity-pair retention and 65.8% versus 7.6% activity-label agreement. Existing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The pose definitions, contrastive objective, and contextual-window formulation are unchanged. The added similarity analysis is empirical and introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the assertion that camera trajectories are privacy-preserving. The abstract also changes trajectories revealing actions to providing valuable cues about them. The central contribution and claims about semantic usefulness, complementary value, and robustness remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new pair analysis as evidence of semantically driven separation beyond geometric similarity. Supplementary Section 3.3 explicitly bounds applicability to everyday human activity videos where camera motion correlates with content. Previously documented subtle-motion, noun-semantics, and pose-estimation failures remain.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section 2.4 adds model variants, prompts, rendered-video and textual-pose input formats, and the fine-tuning dataset for the new baselines. Existing CamFormer implementation details, hardware specifications, and project access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Qwen3 and Qwen3-VL reports, Reading Recognition in the Wild, Seeing in the Dark, and Day2Dark. It newly credits Seeing in the Dark as inspiration for scene-attribute evaluation. The broader research positioning and novelty argument remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized grammar edits, an expanded baseline subsection organized into categories, an additional analysis paragraph, revised limitations, and a funding acknowledgment. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains four rows, main-text caption titles receive stronger typographic emphasis, and supplementary figures and tables are rearranged around expanded text. Existing plots and illustrations are retained; no new numbered figure or table is introduced.

improvement.justification: The direct-trajectory baselines in Table 4 and quantitative geometry-versus-semantics analysis provide useful support beyond v1's narrower comparisons and qualitative embedding illustration. Removing the privacy claim and clarifying applicability improve precision. These are limited gains, with the new fine-tuning and trajectory-alignment procedures still incompletely specified.
